title: Strata Scenarios Prioritizer (SSP) for cycle-aware roadmap slicing
creator: Asha Patil
description:
Purpose: Introduce a compact, cycle-aware prioritization framework (Strata Scenarios Prioritizer, SSP) to help PMs rank initiatives by combined business opportunity and production-economics risk for each planning cycle. SSP is designed to be calculated with signals available from Redwood Console (per-route throughput/latency/cost), usage analytics, and lightweight stakeholder inputs so it can be used in weekly triage and quarterly roadmap planning.

Core idea: Move beyond a single static RICE score by layering scenario (capacity regime) and cycle phase into the score calculation. Each candidate initiative is scored across three orthogonal dimensions and then adjusted by two regime multipliers: CostNormalization and LatencyPenalty. The output is a single scalar (SSP Score) plus a recommended action band for the target cycle.

Components and formulas (textual):
- BaseOpportunity = Reach * Impact * Confidence
  - Reach: estimated affected unique routes/users in the next 90 days (normalized to 0..1 by cohort buckets).
  - Impact: 1..10 estimated benefit to business metric (revenue, retention, latency SLO improvement).
  - Confidence: calibrated percentage (0.0..1.0) reflecting evidence (experiments, telemetry, customer research).
- CostScore: normalized cost-per-1k-token (or compute-hours) for the initiative's expected traffic shape; normalized so baseline model = 1.0. Lower is better.
- LatencyPenalty: multiplicative factor derived from the initiative's expected P90 tail delta vs SLO: examples: <=0ms -> 0.9, 1-10ms -> 1.0, 10-50ms -> 1.2, >50ms -> 1.5.
- PhaseWeight: scalar for cycle phase (Discovery=0.7, Build=1.0, Rollout=1.2). Prioritizes experiments differently across cycle phases.

SSP Score = (PhaseWeight * BaseOpportunity) / (CostScore * LatencyPenalty)

Recommended action bands (example mapping):
- SSP >= 0.8: Commit to Build this cycle (green)
- 0.45 <= SSP < 0.8: Pilot / Scoped Build (yellow)
- 0.2 <= SSP < 0.45: Run Discovery / Experiment (blue)
- SSP < 0.2: Defer / Monitor (gray)

Why different from straight RICE: SSP explicitly folds in deployment capacity regimes (CostScore computed using actual capacity profiles from Dedicated/Dedicated-burst usage and private region cost factors), latency SLO consequences, and cycle-phase weighting so the same initiative can be scored differently depending on whether we are in a growth sprint vs. stabilization cycle. This makes it actionable for both Hosted & Dedicated/Private customers.

Data sources and instrumentation requirements:
- Reach & traffic shape: Redwood Console per-route usage export (last 90 days).
- CostScore: runtime-1.XX cost-per-GPU-hour and per-token cost tables; normalized using our model catalog mappings.
- LatencyPenalty: P95/P99 deltas from canary runs or synthetic benchmarks (benchmark-run doc: https://drive.google.com/example-benchmark-ssr).
- Confidence: PRD evidence + experiment result links.

Operational rules and decision governance:
- Each cycle triage meeting will run SSP on the top 40 candidates and publish a ranked list along with top-3 constraints (capacity, infra risk, security review).
- For initiatives that cross Dedicated/Private boundaries, include region-specific CostScore and present both SSP scores; default to the more conservative (lower) score for enterprise rollouts.
- Ties resolved by strategic alignment tag matching OKR owner and by historical rollout success (success factor multiplier).

Acceptance criteria (what we want before we mark Done):
1) SSP calculator script in repo that consumes Console exports and returns scores for a list of PM submissions. (path: github.com/redwood-inference/pm-ssb/ssp-calculator)
2) Example run with 40 initiatives imported from current backlog and a generated ranked list.
3) Integration test that pulls cost/latency snapshots from staging console and verifies CostScore normalization logic.
4) Triage playbook doc and triage template published in Confluence.
5) PM/Eng/Research sign-off from the first live cycle (email thread + retrospective note).

Notes on transparency and guardrails: keep the SSP formula visible on the Confluence page. All inputs that are manually provided (Impact, Confidence) must be accompanied by a short evidence link. Any initiative with a LatencyPenalty >= 1.2 must include a mitigation plan and an engineering approver before move to Build.
